Alex (runtime): Quick FYI — swapping oncall with Sam tomorrow 09:00-17:00 PT. Leaving handoff notes below.
Alex (runtime): Handoff notes:
- Active experiments: kv-cache prefix test (watch qps & miss rate)
- Known risk: small fleet of a100s in eu-west will be drained for maintenance 11:00-13:00
- If latency spikes, toggle routing to smaller batch size (route policy: latency-prefer)
Priya (sre): Quick clarifying Q — who owns cache evictions and auto-scale tuning during that window?
Alex (runtime): Runtime owns serving runtime behavior (batching, cache logic, model fallbacks). SRE owns infra scaling, node replacement, networking. For escalations: ping @oncall-sre, then infra lead if it's a node-level issue. For P0s page the PagerDuty rotation and the ENG-STANDUP channel.
Sam (oncall): Definition check — we treat as incident if customer-facing latency > 2x SLA for 5+ min, error rate >1% for 5+ min, or any data-loss. Otherwise handle as operational FYI and track in the handoff doc.
Tess (eng): Where's the canonical runbook for these handoffs? I couldn't find the latest version.
Alex (runtime): Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/oncall-handbook (section "runtime vs sre responsibilities") — I updated the checklist last week.
oncall-bot: Reminder: handoff checklist incomplete — load test note missing from Alex's checklist :bell:
Priya (sre): I'll add the load test summary and the infra escalation contact list by EOD. Also adding explicit play for cache thrash.
Sam (oncall): Thanks — appreciated. I'll double-check routing rules before start. :thumbsup:
